newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold lower, but India puts floor on fall.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold lower, but India puts floor on fall.

text.p: Dubai gold prices fell in line with sharply lower international bullion rates in the week to Sunday, but traders said political turmoil in India had helped keep prices in the emirate from slipping further.

"There is good moderate demand from India. Because of the political scene there the market is a bit better than it would have been. It would have been lower if there hadn't been the political upheaval in India," said one trader.
Dubai is the main feeder market for gold into the subcontinent. India is the world's single largest gold market.

New Delhi's 10-month-old minority government was defeated in a parliamentary confidence vote on April 11. The political crisis continued until late Saturday when the United Front alliance named Inder Kumar Gujral as its leader to head a new government.
In times of political uncertainty investors often turn to gold as a safe haven.
Traders said even though some shipments to the subcontinent had been slowed down by the four-day Eid al-Adha Moslem holiday in Dubai, demand was still evident.

This was likely to pick up further as the second Indian wedding season got into full swing and Indians and Pakistani buyers took advantage of weak global prices to stock up on their favourite investment vehicle.
International prices this week tested the four-year lows seen in January and slumped to around $337.50 an ounce, dragging down Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar price with them.
The TT bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders at 4,720-4,725 dirhams ($1,286-1,287) on Sunday, down from 4,795 dirhams on April 13.
On the international market, spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $341.20/$341.90 an ounce, down more than five dollars on the previous week's $346.75/$347.25.
Dubai gold traders said the sharp weakening in bullion in the past week was also expected to help boost local demand as the Dubai Shopping Festival draws to a close.
The World Gold Council expects gold sales of around seven tonnes during the month-long promotion, which ends on April 26.
"As prices are now lower and people have an opportunity to win one kg daily and 10 kg at the end-of-festival draw, we should see retail sales rise," said one Dubai trader.
